findings.title: The new groups line contradicts the set note and the Controls section about what a turn and a pressed turn do
findings.state_task_viewport: Task: answer 'what does a turn or pressed turn do now'. States: dial-configured (three GPU readings) with Gestures Elite, then press Split into groups; dial-groups with Gestures Legacy, and with Custom without a Switch gesture; dial-groups Legacy with Ignore turns. 373x410 DPR 1.5, also 189x410.
findings.observed: After Split on Elite, three visible statements disagree. The set note says '2 groups. They take effect once two of them hold readings; until then rotation runs as one flat list.' The groups line says 'New ticks go to the marked group. Turns stay inside a group; a pressed turn jumps to the next group and shows its name.' The Controls summary and 'What the dial does now' say 'pressed turn switches sensor'. On Legacy (and Custom without a Switch gesture) with both groups filled, the set note says 'Rotation needs two or more readings in a group to move inside it.' The line 60 px below says 'Legacy gestures cannot switch groups, so turns run through all groups as one list, in group order.' On Legacy with Ignore turns, the line still says 'turns run through all groups' while the picker line says 'Turns are ignored here.'
findings.evidence: MEASURED p2\probe2.json split-elite and split-legacy; walk\walk-373.json dial-groups-legacy, dial-groups-custom, dial-groups-onefull, dial-groups-legacy-ignore; crop-dial-groups-legacy.png, crop-dial-groups-onefull.png. Baseline (p3b\probe3.json split-elite): a generic conditional paragraph, and Controls said 'switches sensor or group', so this direct contradiction is new. READ: candidate pi-common.js updateRotationHelp (line 836) derives the line from the stored map only and never checks whether groups are in effect; the set note (lines 1015-1016) ignores the preset. Runtime: src/ui/dial-overview.ts:25-30 (groups steer only when schemeCanSwitchGroups) and src/rotation.ts rotationGroupsOf (two or more groups must hold keys).
findings.affected_user: beginner (the state right after Split is the first thing anyone creating groups sees); screen reader users read both sentences in sequence
findings.correction: Derive the set note and the groups line from one rule: the map can switch groups AND model.groupsActive(settings). While fewer than two groups hold readings, put the line in the future tense ('Once two groups hold readings, turns stay inside a group and a pressed turn jumps between groups.'). When the map cannot switch groups, remove 'Rotation needs two or more readings in a group to move inside it' from the note, because the line already says what happens. With Ignore turns on and no other gesture that jumps, say 'Ignore turns is on; groups only set the order.' Optional: replace 'the marked group' with 'the group with the filled circle'.
findings.tradeoff: Two strings gain a branch, and the R19/R42 e2e strings change. The risk is growing back to several lines; keep it to one note plus one line.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-configured with Elite, press Split: no visible text in #rotation-set or #rotation-help says 'stay inside a group' or 'jumps to the next group' in the present tense while [data-summary=interaction] contains 'switches sensor'. dial-groups with controlPreset legacy, or custom without stepGroup: no visible sentence contains 'move inside it'. With rotationDisabled true on Legacy, #rotation-help does not contain 'turns run'. Opening makes 0 writes.

findings.title: The Check again answer says 'no change yet' even when the answer changed
findings.state_task_viewport: Task: after fixing HWiNFO, ask the panel whether it worked. States: key-unavailable at 373x410, press Check again while the plugin's answer changes (Shared Memory frozen, or the saved reading absent); key-missing, press Reload sensor list.
findings.observed: The status region rebuilds with the new problem (the stale block or the missing-reading block) and ends with 'Checked again at 11:54:41 AM: no change yet. The plugin also reads HWiNFO every 1 s on its own.' On the missing block the button says 'Reload sensor list' but the answer says 'Checked again'. With HWiNFO not running, 'reads HWiNFO every 1 s' overstates what happens (the plugin retries opening it).
findings.evidence: MEASURED p2\probe2.json check-unavail-to-stale, check-unavail-to-missing, check-same-unavailable, check-same-missing, check-same-stale-dial, with PNGs. READ candidate pi-shell.js answerCheck (line 701) writes 'no change yet' whenever a tree answer arrives after the press, including at the end of the rebuilt-box path in renderStatus. It never compares the answer with the problem shown at the press. On the real host previews arrive every tick, so the window is narrow (INFERRED).
findings.affected_user: beginner; screen reader users hear the whole rebuilt block including the false line
findings.correction: Store the status signature at the press. Write 'no change yet' only when the answer's signature matches it; otherwise write nothing (the new lines already speak) or 'Checked again at X: the problem changed.' On the missing block, say 'Reloaded at X: still not in HWiNFO's list.' When the status is unavailable, say 'tries HWiNFO every 1 s'.
findings.acceptance_test: key-unavailable: set the sim data to stale and press Check again; .hw-status-ack does not contain 'no change'. A press with an unchanged answer still gets the timed line. key-missing: the answer line after Reload sensor list does not start with 'Checked again'.

findings.title: Twin tags are identical when HWiNFO's sensor names carry no instance mark, so two drives still look the same
findings.state_task_viewport: Task: tell two 'Drive Temperature' chips apart in the rotation list. Dial with rotationKeys [drive0, drive1, gpu] on a simulated snapshot whose two drive sensors are named 'S.M.A.R.T.: Example NVMe SSD 2TB (S5GXNF0R100001)' and '...100002)'. 373x410.
findings.observed: Both chips read 'Drive Temperature' followed by a tag reading 'Example NVMe …'. Only the tooltip and the screen-reader text tell them apart. By the same rule, 'Samsung SSD 980 PRO 1TB' and 'Samsung SSD 990 PRO 2TB' both shorten to 'Samsung SSD 9…'. With the fixture's '[#0]' and '[#1]' names the tags work ('#0' and '#1').
findings.evidence: MEASURED p2\probe2.json twins-nomark (tag 'Example NVMe …' on both chips) and p2\twins-nomark.png; walk dial-twins for the marked case. READ candidate pi-common.js twinTagOf (line 418): HWiNFO's instance mark, else the text after the last colon cut to 13 characters plus an ellipsis, with no check that the tags differ. INFERRED: HWiNFO names drive sensors like 'S.M.A.R.T.: <model> (<serial>)' without [#N]. If so, drives, the register's own example, take this path, and the fixture's 'Drive [#0]' names hide it.
findings.affected_user: everyone with two same-model or same-brand drives (beginners do not hover)
findings.correction: After computing the tags for a scope, check colliding readings for equal tags. If two are equal, use the shortest distinguishing part (for example keep the end: '…100001)'), or number the twins in HWiNFO's list order in the same pill. Keep the full sensor name in the title and in the screen-reader text.
findings.tradeoff: A synthesized number is not HWiNFO's own mark. Tags that keep the end are longer and may wrap at 189 (the pills already wrap there).
findings.acceptance_test: For any rotation or detail list holding two equal names whose sensors differ (including sensors without [#N] whose names share their first 13 characters), the visible .hw-chip-source texts differ at 373 and 189.
